steps.text: Mix soy sauce, garlic, hot pepper sauce, and ginger together in a large bowl until well combined. Add chicken to the bowl, turn to coat evenly, then cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
When ready to cook, remove chicken from marinade and shake off excess. Reserve marinade in the bowl.

Heat sesame oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add brown sugar and stir until dissolved. Add onion and sauté for 5 minutes. Add chicken; cook and stir until evenly browned, about 5 minutes. Add water and reserved marinade and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add peanut butter, stir until well combined, and simmer for 10 more minutes.
Transfer chicken to a serving platter, then pour sauce over the top. Garnish with green onions.

raw_recipe.headline: Thai Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This mouthwatering Thai chicken is marinated and cooked in a spicy garlic, soy, and ginger mixture with peanut butter added at the very end.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was fabulous! I also reduced the soy sauce to 1/3 cup and I cut the peanut butter down to 2 TBSP. I used 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts cut into small strips. I made it an entire meal by adding broccoli, sliced carrots and strips of green bell pepper, along with the onions already listed in the recipe. Will definitely make this again!

Did not have all of the ingredients and with the COVID-19 atmosphere, didn't want to go out to get stuff. I did see the other reviews about the soy sauce, and took that to heart. I used 1/2 cup low sodium soy sauce and it was perfect. I also got impatient and put all of the ingredients in the marinade. I used ground ginger instead of fresh, and creamy PB instead of crunchy. I had no green onions and had chicken breasts instead of thighs. So with substituting and improvising, it was still a darn good meal. I served over a brown rice and quinoa blend, which helped with the heavy hand I used on the pepper sauce. Ne worries, we like hot . I will do this again, and maybe even follow the recipe a little closer nest time:)

Well, I am not the Thai cooking master but few things were not OK. 1. The chicken is overcooked. After initial frying 5-10 minutes is more then enough. 2. Due to 1. some initial tastes/smells are gone before the end. Peanut taste is overwhelming all others being added last. 3. Maybe lime juice would add some freshness. 4. I will repeat this dish wiith following changes: I will initially fry chicken in brown sugar caramel only, and after that add all other ingredients, for 5-10 minutes cooking

This was tasty with some modifications. Firstly I cut the soy sauce to 1/3 cup to 2/3 cup water. This is CRUCIAL unless you enjoy very salty food. I didn’t have crunchy peanut butter, only natural smooth but I did have unsalted peanuts. I smashed the peanuts and added them along with the 2 1/2 tablespoon of the natural peanut butter. I used sriracha and chili paste instead of the red pepper sauce. We like spicy food in my family so I added plenty. I also added fresh cilantro in addition to the green onions. Scrumptious and flavorful.

I added cashews since I didn't have chunky peanut butter and also added bite size pieces of red bell pepper and fresh broccoli and mushrooms to the skillet for the last 10 min to make this a one dish meal. I didn't have 1 cup of soy sauce, but didn't really need it. Delicious!

Great recipe! I made a few changes and I think it came out really well. Only 3/4 cup of soy sauce and a diced up tomato to make up the difference. Added Indian chili powder and turmeric for color and kick. And I tossed in a bag of frozen whole green beans to cook in the simmer. You can see an uploaded picture.

I had to eventually raise the head because my chicken was still bleeding. I cut back the soy sauce to 1/2 cup and used 3 teaspoons of peanut butter, and added some honey because i found it to be very salty even with the reduced soy sauce. Cooked the green onions for the last 10 minutes with the chicken to add some flavor. Will not be making this again.

After reading everyone's comments, I also only used 1/3 of lite sodium soy sauce and 2/3 cup of chicken stock to make 1 cup. I used boneless/skinless chicken breast sliced before placing in the marinade. Only 3 large cloves of garlic were used. I used 2 tbs of brown sugar as recommended by reviews, but next time I will only use 1 as I don't like it that sweet. I used a Tbl of Siracha sauce instead of hot sauce. Three Tbl crunchy peanut butter were used. It is perfect. It will be even better without the extra sugar.

I enjoyed the recipe but did cut back on soy sauce and used low sodium. I used both chicken thighs and breast meat and let it marinate over night. I think Thai red curry paste would have been better than the hot pepper sauce. I served this over a coconut/nectarine infused rice.

My families and I's new favorite allrecipes.com dish. This dish is very addicting and fairly easy to make. Like most people i reduced the soy sauce to 1/3 of a cup, and the peanut butter to 2-3 tablespoons. I on the other hand only had 1.7pnds of ground turkey on hand, so i followed all the steps but pouring in the marinade since it was completely absorbed by the ground turkey. I also instead used whole bushing of green onion. In addition i used a bushing of mint leaves, and a 1/2-2/3 a cup of bell pepper or carrots thinly sliced for added texture and flavors. Also if you like it really spicy i suggest adding a couply jalepenos cut in quarters or thrids.

Very good, but I did not exactly follow the recipe. Instead of soy sauce I uses Gourmet sauce....found at Costco by the soy sauce. It has way less salt and already has some sweetness, so I skipped the step of adding brown sugar. I used 1/2 cup gourmet sauce, 4 cloves garlic, a little ground ginger, 1/4 teaspoon spicy chili garlic paste and a tablespoon of vinegar for the marinade. I cooked the chicken and wisked 1 tablespoon of peanut butter into the leftver marinade and added that to cook with the browned chicken. The whole family loved it, even the little kids.

The result was OK, but I took the advice of others that said that there was way too much soy sauce so I also reduced it by half. Should have followed the advice to reduce the soy sauce to 1/3 c and add extra water. I also added a variety of vegetables. It was good, but I think I will like it much better with al lot less soy sauce.
I followed the comments and used 1/3 c soy sauce. I added sliced bell peppers and sugar snap peas with the onion. The family loved it
Excellent, my family loves it. The peanut butter is what makes this dish, I make this at least once a month. I am marinating some thighs right now.
Very flavorful, I used cubed chicken breasts rather than thighs. Delicious!
A little to salty for a Thai peanut sauce. But still edible.
Very tasty but very salty, even using low sodium soya sauce. Next time I'll decrease the soya sauce by half and make up the difference with water.
It was a little spicy for my hubs but still got rave reviews! Will do again!

Very good, my Asian relatives thought it took out-LOL
I added shredded carrot and thinly sliced red pepper
I followed the recipe exactly. It came out perfect! One of the best peanut sauces I have made.
